title: Reflection releases Beam, a 501-billion-parameter Apache-licensed coding model
friendlyTitle: A new open coding model you can host yourself
summary: Hugging Face published Reflection's first model on 16 October: Beam, a text-only mixture-of-experts model with 501 billion parameters and about 23 billion active per token, a one-million-token context window, and an Apache 2.0 licence. It is aimed at coding and agent work, and it ships with a Rust harness plus day-one support in transformers, vLLM and SGLang. The BF16 checkpoint is about 1TB.
friendlySummary: Reflection's first model, Beam, is free to use and change under the Apache licence. It has 501 billion parameters, but only about 23 billion are used for each token. It reads and writes text, can handle a very long prompt, and is built for coding agents. The full file is about 1TB.
whyItMatters: Teams that can host a large model can inspect, fine-tune and serve a coding model under a permissive licence instead of renting a closed API. The benchmark table is Reflection's own, and the full checkpoint is a server deployment, not something that runs on a consumer GPU.
friendlyWhyItMatters: A company with its own servers can run and adapt the model instead of paying a closed service. The test scores come from the maker, and this is not a model for a normal home graphics card.
